changes: Dataset created. No profiles have been researched yet. Institutions on an official list are rated High from those lists alone (rubric 1.1), with each listing shown as evidence; institutions on no list are not rated.

Pilot research: the seven Seven Sons of National Defence universities (Beihang, BIT, HIT, HEU, NWPU, NUAA, NJUST) researched and verified with sourced, archived evidence, including documented US export-control and espionage cases; each is rated Very high.

Second research batch: ten PLA bodies on Canada’s NRO list (the Academy of Military Science and its Academy of Military Medical Sciences, and eight PLA Air Force schools) researched and verified with sourced, archived evidence; each is rated Very high.

Third research batch: ten more PLA bodies on Canada’s NRO list (the Air Force Research Institute, the Xi’an flight academy and eight PLA Army schools, including Army Medical University with its hospitals marked for batch-check matching) researched and verified; each is rated Very high.

Fourth research batch: three PLA schools, four bodies Canada and the US list as part of China’s nuclear-weapons complex (CAEP), a CETC research academy listed by the US over surveillance in Xinjiang, and two listed universities (BESTI, BUPT) researched and verified; eight are rated Very high and two High.

Fifth research batch: CAEP itself and China Jiuyuan Trading Corporation, which Canada and the US list as part of it; the PLA’s aerodynamics research centre (CARDC); Dalian Naval Academy; two People’s Armed Police academies (the Coast Guard Academy and PAP Engineering University); two universities run by the Ministry of Public Security (CPPU, CIPUC); and two listed Chinese Academy of Sciences institutes (Shenyang Institute of Automation, Institute of Computing Technology) researched and verified; eight are rated Very high and two High. HPSTAR’s Chinese name moved from CAEP’s record to its own.

The US Section 1286 list (FY2025 edition, published 23 July 2026) and Japan's End User List (revision of 29 September 2025) are now loaded, so no list reads "Not checked yet". 37 institutions are new to the tracker, 14 that were on no other list are now rated High from the 1286 list, and three institutions the US lists named twice are now one record each.

The official lists name academies and institutes of CASC, CASIC and AVIC, not the groups themselves, so each listed unit now has its own record and the groups no longer show as listed (they are not rated until researched); a group's profile names its listed units. Institutions already in the tracker that a list names under a company-style name, such as CAEP's trading companies, now show that list. 11 institutions are new to the tracker, and two that had duplicate records (NIIPKh in Sergiev Posad, FNPC Start) are now one record each.

Sixth research batch: three PLA schools (Information Engineering University, the Army Institute of NBC Defence and the Army Command College in Nanjing), the PAP Logistics University, a national defence key laboratory at NUDT that the US lists (Key Laboratory of Information Systems Engineering), Jiangnan Social University, which Chinese government notices place under the Ministry of State Security, the Ministry of Public Security’s Institute of Forensic Science, USTC’s Hefei national research centre for physical sciences at the microscale, Hunan University and the Nanjing Institute of Information Technology researched and verified; seven are rated Very high and three High.

Seventh research batch: ten PLA bodies on Canada’s NRO list researched and verified: the National Defense University, the National University of Defense Technology and eight PLA Navy schools and research bodies (the Naval Command College, Naval University of Engineering, Naval Aviation University, Naval Medical University with its three hospitals marked for batch-check matching, Navy Submarine Academy, Naval Service Academy, Naval NCO School and Naval Research Academy); each is rated Very high. Five map points were moved to the institutions’ campuses.
